utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) I believe?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can I ask you to have a look at a map.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D4275. 1D4275, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Meanwhile, do you agree, Mr. Witness, that Foca was one of the municipalities of the former Yugoslavia with the largest surface area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in terms of square metres, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how do you view the fact that such a vast municipality should have had too little room for both the Serbs and the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that question is addressed to the wrong person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the right-hand-most side of the map, there where the -- so the very east.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that zoomed in, and can we have the -- can you scroll down, please. Further down, please. There we have it. Foca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: With this irregular shape jutting into Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can it be enlarged further, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be further enlarged, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the villages are more or less clear-cut, they are either Serb or Muslim, though there are a number of mixed villages as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few of them were mixed, in fact. As for the purely Muslim and purely Serb villages, I don't think there were many of those.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But let's say over 75 per cent, 80 per cent were villages that are illustrated in green here which were either Serb or Muslim; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you now recognise which villages these are, perhaps the areas jutting into Montenegro, are they Celebici, or?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the direction of Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you tell that the town itself is quite mixed as well?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please use the electronic pen that the usher will show you and mark for us the areas as they were controlled by the different parties on the 4th and 5th of April?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you the information in relation to villages. I can draw the line in the town proper between Donje Polje and the area held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we zoom in further onto the purple area denoting the urban zone. Where it says "Foca." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you use a blue pen and draw the flow of the Drina across the town, if you can?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be flowing this way in the direction of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that you've missed the entire town.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm looking at these letters as if they were the core of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But don't you think that this purple area is the town centre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this the area you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Drina would then definitely run this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And as for the town itself?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, of course, through the heart of the town. We could say that it runs along the entire town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Where the health centre is, where the bus station is, the municipality building, those areas, under whose control were they when you were there on the 4th and 5th of April?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The area stretching from the health centre to Gornji Ceotinski bridge all the way to Donji Ceotinski bridge, along the Ceotina river, that area was held by the Muslims. Now, the area complete with the bus station and everything else was held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And that was the case when you left on the 12th; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I left on the 12th, the town had fallen. So I don't know about that. So if it had fallen, it means that it wasn't liberated and that there weren't any Muslims in that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's be more specific: The urban core and the general down-town area was held by Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how did the town fall? How did it come about? Who attacked the town centre?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Serbs did from the neighbouring hills, from the hills overlooking the town, until the soldiers got into town. This was some 100 to 200 metres away from my home that I saw soldiers walk in, strolling in. Now, as for the areas further away from my neighbourhood, when they fell, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's clarify for the Trial Chamber: Donje Polje is an area of town further down the river; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the urban core of Foca had been controlled by the Serbs all along, from the beginning; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, who attacked the town, then?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Serbs did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How would they be able to attack themselves?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They attacked the part of town that was held by the Muslims. As for the urban core, Donje Polje and all the areas bordering the central Foca had been inhabited by Muslims but they had left by that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, the Serbs controlled something that could be called Foca proper, or Foca town, so the centre of town. As the fighting developed, the Serbs weren't able to attack Foca because they controlled the major part of the town, did they not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a part of town they did. There were -- there was an area that was held by the Muslims. And the central area that we mentioned was held by the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I don't know if this map was helpful at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think it will assist the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do agree. We will not be tendering it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, after your testimony and your mention of Mr. Ostojic, the OTP conducted an interview with Velibor Ostojic, who has passed away in the meantime. I'd like to remind you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it's 1D4441, for those who would like to refer to it. In e-court, 1D-- oh, I'm sorry, it hasn't been uploaded yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We looked at it when you mentioned Mr. Ostojic, but it's not been uploaded yet. Let me remind you: Mr. Ostojic said to Ms. Karsten that this is something that he never said, at page 37 of the interview, that he had never said that and that he absolutely denied ever saying words that were attributed to him. What do you have to say to that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's his private statement. And as for my statement, I stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He says that, at the time, he attend the funeral of his father at Borje, near Celebici, and that that was not his usual rhetoric. And would you agree that it wasn't, because he was a professor of languages and literature, a man of repute?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was precisely these men of repute who demonstrated the fact that they've lost all their dignity. I stand by what I said. I have nothing further to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you heard other people hear that; right? You didn't hear it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard his voice myself as I was at my neighbour's, precisely as I explained it in my evidence. I had occasion to hear his voice on television, radio, et cetera. What I told you yesterday was the context behind the meeting of the SDS with the municipal leadership, i.e., a president of the Assembly, president of the Executive Board. That was something that I heard, that he walked into the meeting and stated what I said in my statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Fortunately, the two who had occasion to hear it are still alive and well, and we'll be able to hear them.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, Mr. Ostojic testified in the Krajisnik case. He was meant to testify in this case as well, unfortunately he passed away. The Defence will kindly ask that Mr. Ostojic's evidence from the Krajisnik case be admitted under 92 quater, if you find good grounds for it. Thank you, Mr. Witness, I've exhausted my 15 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, I don't think Mr. Karadzic meant to file that motion orally now. I think that it's coming in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. You've already indicated you don't want to receive those motions until the Defence case commences, so we'll do it at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff, do you have any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. Nothing arises.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, sir. That concludes your evidence. On behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal as a whole, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague again. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank. We will break for your convenience. And we'll about -- for 5 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Just one point, and that relates to the document that was yesterday MFI'd, and that is 1D4429.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: We have meanwhile located the full version, and Mr. Reid has uploaded it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And do we have the full translation as well?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: No, there was no translation to it. So it -- but what my proposal would be, to replace the short version that was tendered yesterday with the full version which shows exactly where it comes from and first page to last page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How extensive is the full version, how many pages?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: It's just one more page in the beginning and I think a few pages at the end. So it's not extensively bigger, but I didn't really -- I wasn't really able to check because I only received this information just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Will you kindly take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please make yourself comfortable. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, president.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Can we begin with a quick formality: Can you state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: My name is Asim Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please be asked to come closer to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. -- I believe you heard that, Mr. Egrlic. If you can --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Perhaps the usher can assist in moving the witness's chair a bit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, we'll take a break every hour, and please don't hesitate to let us know if you need a break at any time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, can you confirm that you have testified before this Tribunal on previous occasions, in particular in the case of Prosecutor versus Krajisnik on the 27th through the 30th of July, 2004.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, the Krajisnik testimony, as the court is aware, is 65 ter 22085.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Egrlic, can you confirm that you have reviewed that testimony, that it accurately reflects your testimony to the Tribunal, and that you would provide the same evidence to the Court if asked about the same matters today.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would tender 22085.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3570, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I can either proceed to read the summary, Mr. President, or to address any issues related to associated exhibits. As the Court prefers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I'm going to read a brief summary of your evidence. It doesn't purport to capture all of your evidence or to be evidence itself, it's just a quick summary.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The witness was a member of the SDA and president of the Executive Board of the SDA in Kljuc municipality. His evidence covers activities and members of the SDA and SDS in Kljuc. Leading figures in the Kljuc SDS included Veljko Kondic and Jovo Banjac. Vinko Kondic, a relative of Veljko Kondic, was chief of the SJB. In addition, the witness discusses the MBO, the Muslim Bosniak association, which was headed by Omer Filipovic. Mr. Egrlic describes events leading to the take-over of Kljuc on the 7th of May, 1992, when flags of the Serbian Republic were placed on buildings, including Kljuc's incorporation by SDS authorities into the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the arrival in Kljuc of JNA units, SDS demands for change of police insignia, and heightened anxieties and fears of the Muslim population. The witness also discusses events after the take-over, including dismissal of Muslims from employment, restrictions on movement, demands for disarming of non-Serbs, and, commencing in late May, attacks on Muslim villages by Bosnian Serb forces, expulsion of Muslims from Kljuc, and destruction of mosques. The witness also discusses the relationship between the local SDS authorities and the regional and republic level SDS or RS leadership, including with regard to the implementation of policy to move people to achieve a limited presence of minorities. The witness himself was arrested on 28 May 1992 and taken to the police building and to Stara Gradiska prison. He was beaten at both locations. He was ultimately transferred to Manjaca, and finally to Batkovic camp. The witness also describes the requirement imposed by RS authorities to relinquish property to the state in order to escape the dangerous circumstances, and of mass graves in Kljuc containing the bodies of Muslim victims of the attacks on villages by the Bosnian Serb forces. That concludes the summary, Mr. President. I have a very few additional questions for Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just one question, Mr. Tieger. I checked the 92 ter transcript, 22-- Exhibit P3570. I see Judge Agius, seems to be Brdjanin. Could you sort it out in the meantime. You are tendering Krajisnik transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I take it that can be corrected. Let's proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'll check both the numbers and the submissions, of course. I don't think there was any misunderstanding among the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, as indicated, I had a very few additional questions for you. First, I'd like you to look at the photographs in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President and Your Honours, I'm asking the witness to look at a hard-copy set of eight photographs depicting a cemetery in Velagici and individual headstones in the cemetery. One of those eight photographs, as indicated in the hard copy, is already in evidence as P00618. The 65 ter numbers of the seven remaining photographs are 65 ter 23473 through -79. They are not on the Prosecution's 65 ter list and we're seeking leave to add those. I have discussed this matter with the Defence and they have no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That's granted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just to be perfectly clear: We want to use this hard copy for demonstrative purposes, and we'll seek admission of the actual individual photographs, which are uploaded in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, turning your attention to these photographs. We see a number of headstones, including a headstone for someone aged 93; someone aged 90; someone of the age of 85; someone of the age of 80; someone of the age of 71; of a woman, Selva Draganovic; and of a 5-year-old child, Denis Becirovic. First of all, Mr. Egrlic, we see above those names the word "Sehid"; can you tell us what that refers to on those tombstones?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Let me first say that these are photographs of headstones that were placed on the graves in Velagici where people were buried who had been found at Laniste, in a locality known as Babina Dolina. They were exhumed there and buried here, hence the headstones, and we can tell that these were victims of various ages, from children, women, to the elderly. The term "Sehid" means that these were victims of war. In other words, these people were killed during the war and they died a violent death, which is something that sets them apart from the other deceased in the cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Egrlic. I know that you indicated in your evidence that you attended exhumations in Kljuc - that's as 4810 through -14. Let me ask you, then: When you say that people -- people in the graves at Velagici who were buried had been found at Laniste at a location at Babina Dolina and they were exhumed, is that a reference to one of the mass graves found in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. There were two mass graves at Laniste, one in Bezdana cave and the other in a valley called Babina Dolina. In the latter, they had been buried by earth-moving machinery; and in the former, rubbish was thrown atop of them. As they were exhumed, autopsies were conducted and then they were buried in the cemeteries closest to their native areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you learn where those people had been killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I learned that these individuals from Velagici had been killed at the very site where now they lie buried, where a primary school used to be located. From there they were transported by trucks to a location some 10 kilometres away, where they were placed in a mass grave, and I'm speaking about Babina Dolina. Likewise, in the village of Biljani, the local population was shot, executed, loaded onto trucks, and transported to a cave at Laniste. It is the so-called Bezdana cave; bottomless, in other words. Some 25 metres deep. Subsequently, they were given a proper burial, the former ones in Velagici and the latter ones in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I tender 23473 through -79.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: They will be admitted. We shall give just one number --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- if you agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for the record: I think this will be corrected, but on page 14, line 12, it's -- the last word is, here, listed as "Bijeljina," but I believe the witness said "Biljani."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the photographs will be Exhibit P3571.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we can call up P03514 MFI.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: As this is being called up, Mr. Egrlic, I just note that this is a document dated the 21st of July, 1992, a decision of the War Presidency of the Municipal Assembly of Kljuc, on the termination of employment of all employees who have failed to respond to the general mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, this is former 65 ter 00848, if that's of any assistance. Let's try the number again: P03514 MFI.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It was noted as just "514."

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I know you've had an opportunity to see this document previously. Can I ask you, first, whether the contents of this document are consistent with what happened in Kljuc regarding terminations of the employment of Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The document says -- refers to termination of all employees. Can you tell the Court whether in Kljuc employees of both Muslim and Serb nationality were terminated or not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, all the Muslims were laid off. Their employment was terminated. And I don't know a single case of a Serb being dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, this document is dated the 21st of July, 1992. Can you tell us whether the termination of employment of Muslims commenced thereafter or whether it had been on-going previously and this document refers to events that have already taken place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that the majority of Muslims had been dismissed towards the end of May, which means that approximately up until the 1st of June most of them had lost their jobs. This decision is dated the 21st of July, 1992, and basically it covered retroactively what had already been effected.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd like to next call up 65 ter 23482. This is a 28 October 1992 decision on terminating the employment of Enisa Filipovic as of 27 May 1992. And, Mr. President, we would seek leave to add this to the 65 ter list as well. Again, I've discussed this with the Defence and there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I understand you've had an opportunity to see this document as well, previously. Can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- whether this document is related to the previous document you just saw and whether it is another example of a --

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And does this also relate to a termination that had already taken place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. One can see from the document, because it says so, that the employment was terminated on the 27th of May, 1992, and the document was drafted on the 28th of October, 1992, with a reference to the decision that we previously saw of the 21st of July, 1992. Therefore, this document also refers to something that had already taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I tender 23482, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Before we come to that document, I should ask Mr. Robinson: When we marked for identification the previous document, Exhibit P3514, and my record shows it's P3490 all MFI'd, Mr. Karadzic's submission was unclear as to whether Defence is challenging the authenticity of those documents or not. While he's said that the contents may have been falsified, he said he would not challenge the document. Could you expand on that?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, it was my understanding that Dr. Karadzic did challenge the document which was -- which bore a stamp but no signature from Kljuc. And it was challenging the authenticity of that. Subsequently, the Prosecution showed another document which the next -- which was the previous number in the serial, which also had a stamp and did have a signature but was not -- the signature was not identified as anyone's, and so I think he also intends to maintain the objection of authenticity as to that document as well. So it's for the Chamber, I think, to determine whether or not there's sufficient circumstances of indicia of authenticity to decide whether to grant or overrule his objection, but I think he wishes to maintain the objection of authenticity to those two documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would simply note in that regard that when asked by the Court about that, the accused didn't make reference to signatures but did say that he considered that this document, 117, which is numbered 117, should have been sent to some companies. Now we see, in fact, the document that does illustrate precisely that, that the document was sent to the company with a specific reference to the decision of July 21st. So in considering the determination of admissibility, of course, we would ask the Court to take that into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Robinson, as to the admission of this document, 65 ter number 23482?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we don't have an objection to this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3572, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, so you're going to raise this issue of marked for identification later on, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- by the evidence of this witness you move to admit those documents in full?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We do renew that position and that proffer based on the arguments previously made, based upon the additional evidence presented today, and we can -- we're in the Court's hands. I think they should be admitted forthwith. But if the Court wants further argument, we can provide that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider that, consider your motion, Mr. Tieger. Please proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And can we next call up 65 ter 23472. Again, Mr. President, we ask leave to add 23472. This is a number of documents of precisely the same type that are, in fact, related to one of the associated exhibits that we anticipate will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, in your earlier testimony, you referred to 65 ter 00864, which was the record of the Kljuc municipal commission for gathering information on resettlement of population, which referred to your wife's departure from Kljuc and what happened to the family's property. That's at transcript page 4766. And you also testified that this was something that had to be done by everyone who had immovable property because it was a precondition for leaving Kljuc municipality. Now, I know you've seen the various records contained in this exhibit. If you look at the first one, referring to Mr. Sistek, can you first confirm you had a chance to look at the other nine records, and tell us whether they're consistent with your information that the same declaration that your wife had to make had to be made by all Muslims in Kljuc as a precondition for departing?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. First I saw the document signed by my wife, and after that I saw the other documents as well. I know that all the Bosniaks who had to leave the municipality of Kljuc signed, under duress, a declaration stating that they would leave all their immovable property to Republika Srpska because that was a precondition for them to be allowed to depart from the area of Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And so when the document says, as it does in the declaration relating to your wife, that "my family and I are leaving Kljuc municipality voluntarily," is that accurate or not? Were people leaving voluntarily?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is not true. Everybody left under coercion. It was a matter of life and death, and people decided to relinquish their property. Regardless of what it says here, that they did it voluntarily, that is not true, because they were forced to do that. And people left their property in this manner in order to save their lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That concludes my examination-in-chief, Mr. President. And I would tender 23472.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And shall we deal with the associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are there any objections, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a couple of items, Mr. Tieger. 65 ter number 21002 and -3, those are maps of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I know exactly what you mean, Your Honour. I realised that those were, sort of, admitted on the basis of consensus, but I also consider that, given the nature of those documents, that they should not present any kind of a problem. I think they were acknowledged as part of the evidence, and I think that was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: -- Mr. Robinson's point as well in not objecting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it was not put to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I agree, but I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So except for those two, everything -- but is it not in evidence already?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The maps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I don't show a reflection of that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see. Let us upload 21002 and -3. I don't think that's necessary. And the next one, 21003. If you'd like to tender them, could you explore with the witness whether he agrees with it, the locations marked on this map, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you see the map of Kljuc municipality in front of you. Taking -- I appreciate it's just a quick look, but if you can see the locations marked, and they'll be blown-up now, if you can indicate to us whether that appears to be generally an accurate representation of the location of those particular designated villages and areas.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, this is Kljuc municipality with all its neighbourhoods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we now have basis to admit those two maps, both of them. All the associated exhibits will be admitted into evidence and given numbers in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would simply note so there's no misunderstanding about it: There was reference to 65 ter 21015, a statement of Mr. Filipovic, in the course of the testimony. We did not include that as an associated exhibit because of the Court's position on statements. But I didn't want there to be any misunderstanding with the Defence or the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's noted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. President, the correct 65 ter number of the Krajisnik testimony is 65 ter 22085A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Egrlic, your testimony in the Krajisnik trial has been admitted in lieu of your examination-in-chief, and now you will be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Would you like to take a break before Mr. Karadzic's cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, please, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll take a break for 20 minutes. --- Break taken at 10.04 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Are you ready? For your planning purpose, today, for the remainder of the day, we'll have two one-hour sessions and two half-an-hour breaks. And, Mr. Egrlic, probably you heard this, but please bear in mind that since yours and Mr. Karadzic's questions have to be translated, please put a pause between the question and answer. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Egrlic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today you spoke about the certificates issued to people and you said that they constituted a hand-over of immovable property to Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up the document that refers to Mr. Sistek. Let us see what it says exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whilst we're waiting, Mr. Egrlic, do we agree that in our country there used to be a category of socially owned flats?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that a person was given a flat, either from his company or some other institutions, for life-long occupation, and that even entitled their children to use it after their death?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Usually these flats were used nearly for a lifetime of the tenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, until recently the ownership over such flats was of those who had built them, that is to say, the work organisation or an institution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Only recently a tenant was given an opportunity to buy the flat and convert it into his private property; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have, now, 11248, 65 ter. But it's actually now a P exhibit, admitted today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you find anywhere in this document a confirmation that this gentleman is doing anything else other than returning the socially owned flat to -- to the company in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, basically he is returning it under extraordinary circumstances, because he was being expelled from Kljuc municipality. Otherwise he wouldn't be forced to return it. I personally know Mr. Sistek; he was a lawyer who worked for the Sip Kljuc company and on that basis was allocated the flat for his personal use. However, when he had to leave the municipality, this flat was taken away from him by force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, please, let us both refrain from making any characterisations and qualifications, and focus on the essence. For example, if you -- if you had a socially owned flat and under certain circumstances you had to leave the company, you would have to return the flat if it was a flat allocated to specific personnel?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this person giving any of his private property to anyone?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Not this person. But there were a number of cases in which people had to leave their houses, their land, their estates, and sign that they were allegedly leaving it behind voluntarily, but that was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, let us see what it was that your wife signed when she was leaving Kljuc. Is it true that she signed the declaration that she was placing the property at the disposal of the municipality? This is not your wife's declaration, but we'll find it shortly, because it was mentioned in examination-in-chief. Do you remember that it says "at the disposal"? Can that be equated with ownership?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, you can construe it in that. If you have a right to dispose of, then you are entitled to dispose of it in every form and shape.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But disposal means the use; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, if you leave something behind without being certain that you would ever come back, that means a permanent relinquishment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave aside the document or the decisions that are issued on the 19th of August that rescinded all these decisions, and you needn't have known about that decision at all. When you returned to Kljuc in 1995, did you register any changes of ownership and any changes of private ownership in cadastre or books that were converted into the property of Republika Srpska, a state that you indicated as someone who was conducting expropriation of private property?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of any such transactions being registered in the cadastre books.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, could you help us, help me, in reading the -- in understanding this statement. Could you read the second statement [sic] in the statement. I read, in English translation: "When moving out, the keys are to be returned to the landlord." Do you see that sentence? Why don't we zoom up the B/C/S part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What does it mean? Who is the landlord?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if we are talking about socially owned flat, the landlords were socially owned companies, because they built those flats and allocated them to their employees for use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But the first sentence says that -- are we seeing the same document? Why don't you upload 65 ter 11248. Is it coming? 11248.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The first sentence in that statement says that: "I hereby state that I own immovable property."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So if you read those two sentences, how should we understand the second sentence, "When moving out, the keys are to be returned to the landlord"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't know. This is about a forceful eviction of a person from his flat, which, basically, if he had an opportunity, he would have been able to buy it after so many years of living there, and he would have been able to do the same if he returned to Kljuc, given that there was no change of ownership. So this is a very complex form of ownership relations. In one part it seems that he owns the flat, whereas on the other hand the company that allocated the flat to him is entitled to dispose of it at any given time. However, we are not talking about his returning the flat to the company. It's not the company that is requesting that, but, rather, an administration organ is doing that, the organ that basically has nothing to do with that flat. It would have been understandable if Sip Kljuc, the company where this gentleman worked, requested that due to some other circumstances. However, under these circumstances, this constituted a forceful confiscation of the flat by the municipality of Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Egrlic. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Egrlic, this is not correct. Please see that he's returning the keys to the landlord, but not the apartment itself. He returns the keys to the landlord so that somebody else could be using the apartment; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's what it says. However, in practice, what happened was that property was forcefully confiscated and the administrative organ of the Kljuc municipality then disposed of it, that was the Serbian municipality, and they could allocate the apartments to whomever they liked, which indeed happened. There were cases that people did not even move out but then by force somebody else would move into the apartment to live there and the person did not even have the chance to take away the property, perhaps just a bundle of things, and this is how they would leave the apartment and give over the key. We are talking about war time conditions rather than conditions in which someone voluntarily left Kljuc, moved away to some other place to live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, I feel uncomfortable to remind you that you gave an oath that you would be telling the truth, but I have to remind you. Do you say that all these papers needed to be collected so that the preconditions would be met for someone to be allowed to leave Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. All of that was necessary. That was the condition for anyone to leave Kljuc. Even in addition to this, one would have to pay electricity or telephone bills, taxes, or anything else that was outstanding as if the person was permanently leaving of his or her own will, but actually this would be a case of someone being forcefully evicted from the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm inviting you to say particularly what do you mean by "forcibly"? If you are waiting for a convoy and looking for connections to be on a list, what is forcible there, what forces you, fear or something else?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, fear and also the organs, because they say if someone says that he wants to leave because he is afraid for his life, then the municipal organs would tell him, Bring such and such a form. And then he would have to address this commission and allegedly relinquish his own property voluntarily and then he would be put on a trailer truck as cattle and driven towards Travnik up to Vlasic. And then what would happen there is that he would be waited there by Serbian soldiers who would then rob him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that what happened to you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That was what happened to my wife.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, your wife is not testifying. You are testifying. So let us be specific. Someone is afraid for his life and requests to be allowed to leave Kljuc. In Kljuc there are obstacles placed before him by the municipality - provide the forms, pay for electricity, taxes, and so on - and then once he settles all that, he can do that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What forces him to leave Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Everything forces him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it fear?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it includes fear, because there were murders and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. When you returned in 1995, did you find a single property relationship which had been changed and registered in the cadastre books or in the court? Were there any illegal changes of property?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I can say that for my own property, because my wife forcibly relinquished it, and there was no change of property in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was no change?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Today you talked about dismissals which were issued five or six months after the event. Are you aware that during war time there is military obligation and also a working obligation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that, for example, a judge whose document we saw here worked from the 27th of May until the 28th of October and then was issued a dismissal?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that the majority of Bosniaks were dismissed by the 1st of June and that practically during the month of June these documents were collected, as we saw earlier, and they were forcibly evicted from the territory of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please let us not go back to your qualifications, because that brings us to the beginning and we then have to distinguish between your qualifications so as to define what is "forcibly." We already did that, so please do not use qualifications, but tell us about events and the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do not qualify witness's evidence, Mr. Karadzic. Let's continue. But in the meantime, do you tender this document, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's already admitted. It's a P document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm afraid it's not.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3573, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I'm asking you now, Mr. Witness, is to establish what happened rather than how we would call it, because if you do that, then you bring me back to the beginning. So from the 27th of May did the Judge work from that date until the 28th of October, or did she stop working on the 27th of May?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: She stopped working on the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the dismissal was issued to her only on the 28th of October; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So was she dismissed or did she dismiss herself?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: She was dismissed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But why didn't they hand over the dismissal to her immediately, but, rather, five months later?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that. I don't have an answer to that. I can just comment on it. That was the case with me as well. I was in a camp, and in my document it said that I worked until a specific date. And the reason, they said, was that I did not report for work and reportedly for that the same persons who imprisoned me in the camp terminated my employment because they said that I did not report for work. I mean, really, what are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when did you stop reporting for work, on the 7th of May; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I stopped on the 7th of May when the municipality was occupied.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you claim that on the 27th of May that was not the key date in your municipality by five or six major incidents which occurred and were directed against the Serbian policemen, Serbian soldiers, and Serbian civilians?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Just how many questions are embedded in this inquiry? And I think they need to be broken down to have any prospect of an intelligible response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, you observe the difficulties or the problems of compound questions. Why don't you put question one by one. In the meantime, Court Deputy could approach the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, was the 27th of May a critical day which is well known because of several incidents?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So between the 7th and the 27th of May, when perhaps you couldn't report for work, you spent these 20 days somewhere. Where were you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I was registered as being on annual leave because I had not used it earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you did not request annual leave, they just registered you as being on annual leave so that they wouldn't dismiss you; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I did not ask for annual leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when they saw that you were not reporting for work in these 20 days, were they entitled to dismiss you after five days?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, if these had been normal circumstances. But I was banned from entering the municipality. We are talking about war time rather than about peacetime conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we'll go back a bit to the beginning of the whole situation. You were a member of the SDA. You were probably one of the founding members of the SDA in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: One of the founding members, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say in several occasions that up until the crisis you had very good co-operation with the SDS, that you distributed power and reached agreements about a majority of issues; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You further say that you agree that there should not be out-voting when important issues that were of vital importance for the people were voted about; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was something that you were interested in at the municipal level where you constituted the minority; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you and your party advocate the same principle at the level of the republic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know when the crisis arose and when were relations between the Serbs and the Muslims and the two leading parties disturbed? You connect that with the date when the Autonomous Region of Krajina was set up; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was declared in early September or maybe even on the last few days in August?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's possible that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you remember that this happened once the historic agreement between the Serbs and the Muslims was cancelled and the MBO, your coalition partner in Kljuc, had been involved in these negotiations with Izetbegovic and that the entire month of August these discussions were taking place?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm aware that there was some initiative, but I do not know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you remember that for the sake of this agreement we gave up any idea of regionalisation and any autonomies in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do not remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, would you agree with me that both the Autonomous Region of Krajina and Kljuc are located deep within Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you then agree with me that what was happening in the Kljuc municipality would have to be related to what was happening in Bosnia-Herzegovina, as a whole, and in Yugoslavia, as a wider whole?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask you to ask me a specific question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the specific question: You say - and you discuss that in 65 ter 22085, on page 6111; that was your testimony in the Stanisic and Zupljanin case - where you say that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was a para-state and that a country has to control its own territory and that this was a para-state; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that a conference on Bosnia-Herzegovina was held and that up until the Dayton there was not a single day on which some conference was being held? We were at conferences on Bosnia all the time.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There were many conferences.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that you first heard about the establishment of Republika Srpska in the second half of 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, do you remember that we mentioned our Assembly for the first time on the 15th of October at a session of the Joint Assembly when we were out-voted about the declaration of the sovereignty of Bosnia? And our deputies then left the Assembly, they walked out of the session.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: What is the question there?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that up until the 15th of October Republika Srpska did not exist? There was even no Assembly of the Serbian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I think that it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you agree that we founded the Assembly of the Serbian People on the 24th of October, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot talk about exact dates. This is something I do not know. I know that it was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the Assembly of the Serbian People only in December, on the 21st of December, announced that it would establish Republika Srpska, or, rather, a Serbian Republic within Bosnia-Herzegovina, unless the request for independence was withdrawn; this took place on the 21st of December?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that Republika Srpska was proclaimed on the 9th of January, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the constitution came into force only on the 27th of March, 1992, whereas the republic became functional in April?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: You're asking me about things that I cannot confirm with any certainty because I was not involved in - how should I call them? - these circles that were in the know. I can confirm the events that took place in Kljuc.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Egrlic, with all due respect, we need to contextualise the events in Kljuc by referring to the general background of the events in Bosnia and Yugoslavia; do you agree?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When was the Bosnian municipality of Kljuc proclaimed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was merely an idea and remained an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it not proclaimed in late 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. It had never been proclaimed, although there was the idea to do so because there were no other options for the future life in the area. People suggested that if no other way was possible, a municipality should be proclaimed of a Muslim majority and that this would be the way on. However, this never came about simply because there were no conditions in place for the citizens to voice their minds on this issue through a referendum. That's why it remained an idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do there exist now a Bosnian and Serbian municipality of Kljuc in that the Serbian one is called Ribnik?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Egrlic, would it not have been better to have done that without going through the war, and the Serbs would have had their part of town and their villages and the Muslim's theirs?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, this was precisely our proposal. But the Serbs refused to to so. They wanted to chase us all out, which is what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is not correct, Mr. Egrlic. You wanted to annex Kljuc to the Cazin Krajina, to Bihac; is that not right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, that's not right. We always considered Kljuc as part of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we do so today, just as we do view Banja Luka; it is part of that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not correct that for the most part Kljuc was part of the association of municipalities of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the case during the SFRY, because Banja Luka was the regional, economic, and administrative capital for the municipalities in the region that were part of the chamber of commerce.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And when the association of municipalities proclaimed itself an autonomous region, you did not wish it to continue having that same status; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is right; we didn't want to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, you wanted to change the status of Kljuc within Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, not. You wanted to turn it into a state, one where no other peoples would be entitled to remain in the area. It's for that reason that the Bosniaks refused it. It was an attempt to create a para-state within Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Witness, about others being disenfranchised of their rights there is something we'll get back to later. But do you know that at the conference in Bosnia-Herzegovina we were given the right to have our own republic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for these statements of yours, don't you think you ought to know what sort of rights we were given in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know what exactly we are talking about. Can you be more to the point?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you were, after all, a functionary of your own party. You write about spending time frequently in Sarajevo. You were in the loop, informed by your party. Didn't you know that the Serbs were against the secession of Bosnia-Herzegovina and had constitutional mechanisms at their disposal to avert any such attempts?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Secession from what? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From Yugoslavia. Who did Bosnia-Herzegovina secede from? Wasn't Bosnia within Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Didn't Bosnia want -- or, rather, part of Bosnia, the Muslim and Croat coalition, want to secede from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, a referendum was held on that issue for the citizenry, which voted in favour of independence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait a moment. Are you familiar with constitutional law? You did study law, did you not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In that case, this is my question: Didn't Muslim and Croat communes want to leave - well perhaps not all the Muslims - to leave Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, Yugoslavia disintegrated with the departures -- the departure of Slovenia and Croatia. There was no Yugoslavia anymore by that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's not up to us to judge that. Wasn't Bosnia within Yugoslavia up until the 6th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that based on the principal of constituency and on two-thirds principle the Serb People was -- in Bosnia were always able to prevent the secession of Bosnia from Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I am not a lawyer and am not able to judge that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we with agree that within the Bosnian Assembly there were 240 deputies?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Possibly. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree that the Republika Srpska Assembly was made up of 73 of out of 86 Serbs who were deputies in the BH Assembly? To this day, Republika Srpska Assembly has 83 deputies.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is 83 more than one-third compared to the total of 240?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that the requirement for a positive outcome of the referendum was that there should be a turnout of two-thirds plus one voter out of the entire electorate?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Which referendum are we referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The referendum which was held in late February and on the 1st of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the requirement was and how many, in fact, turned out. I know that a majority was required and that on this basis a vote was cast in favour of the country's independence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, two-thirds did not turn out. And of those who did, 62 per cent voted. And even in that case --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Again, I'm struggling to understand the relevance of these issues. How you come to a war is not that relevant, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, with all due respect, this witness, as well as others, in ambitious 92 ter documents provided by the OTP speak to a host of issues and give their accounts of the events seen through the loop of their political views. What I want to get from this witness is to confirm that Kljuc was in Bosnia-Herzegovina and that the events in Kljuc were related to the events in Bosnia-Herzegovina in general. That's the main point.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Secondary, Mr. Egrlic, do you know that that the constitution can be amended only in a constitutional way, through a constitutional procedure?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know how a constitution is amended. I'm not a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that you were opposed to any sort of out-voting. You said that this is something that you referred to, for instance, in 22085 at page 6108. Does this also relate to the Serbs in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that nobody has the right to outvote them and amend the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina in an unconstitutional -- in a counter-constitutional way? Just answer that question. Weren't the Serbs entitled to the protection of their constitution?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, in my view, there should be no out-voting anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did not Kljuc ultimately take a decision to become part of the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the president of municipality Banjac and the municipality itself defer the implementation of this decision for the sake of preserving good relations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Kljuc municipality have representatives in the Assembly of the autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall who it was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, do you remember, that it was the vice-president of Kljuc municipality, Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll find the reference later. You said that there emerged a crisis in your relations at a point when we proclaimed the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and this you tied in with the plebiscite as well. When did the Serbs hold the plebiscite in favour of staying within Yugoslavia? Or let me help you: Do you agree that it was on the 10th and 11th of November?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you agree that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was proclaimed perhaps on the last day of August or early September, in other words, two months before the plebiscite?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you also agree that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was a region within Bosnia-Herzegovina and did not raise any calls for its departure from Yugoslavia [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're talking about 1991. Are you saying that the Autonomous Region of Krajina asked that it should not be in Bosnia or that it should stay within Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know if they voiced any requests. I only know that they broke off all contact with organs of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and that they strove towards maintaining contact only with the organs in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree, Mr. Witness, that both a proclamation of your Bosnian municipality of Kljuc and the Serbian autonomous districts were empty declarations which did not become fully functional before the war broke out, before the secession of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, the bodies of the autonomous region did become functional before then. Certain decisions were taken which were honoured by municipality bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's look at what you said in 2208 -- I'm sorry, no, in the Brdjanin case, at page 10545. I'll be reading in English: [In English] "You as a Muslim in a municipality that was taken into this new separatist commune, how was that, did you think, going to affect your personally -- you personally as a Muslim, if at all? "A. Since a referendum of the Serbian people was held and that they came out in favour of staying within Yugoslavia, this new parastate did not guarantee that the Muslims would enjoy all of their rights as citizens and for that reason we did not want to accept to remain part of the autonomous region, and that is why we pointed out that ... we wished to form a separate municipality and that we were citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina and that we wanted to be a part of ... state." [Interpretation] Therefore, do you agree that the Autonomous Region of Krajina was proclaimed in late August or early September and that the plebiscite of the Serb people was held on the 10th and 11th of November?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that all the way to the 9th of January --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, a small correction. At 42/21, the -- Mr. Karadzic, I think inadvertently, omitted the second-to-last word of the passage he was quoting from. He read "part of state." It should say "that state," according to the transcript he was reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Of that state." [Interpretation] Yes, I agree, "of that state." Can I have your leave to call up a document that I haven't announced simply because I didn't know that the examination will take the course it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that political life in Bosnia-Herzegovina was at a stand still on the 15th of October because the Muslim Croat coalition passed a constitutional decision to change the character of the state, but it did so in a counter-constitutional way; there was an impasse at that point, therefore?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember a crisis setting in. But as for the other qualifications that you mentioned, I cannot confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the next page, 10546, you were asked when the crisis started and when those relations broke, and you say: [In English] "They were disrupted in such a way that the Municipal Assembly did not work the way it did before and it was difficult to reach certain decisions." [Interpretation] And your previous answer was: [In English] "As far as the referendum is concerned, most of the Serbs came out in favour of joining Yugoslavia or in favour of remaining in the former Yugoslavia, and then from that day on our relationships in the political life of the municipality of Kljuc were disrupted."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With the Chamber's leave, I would like to call 31968, 65 ter document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the name of Rasim Kadic, the president of the liberal party?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let's see what kind of telephone conversation took place between Rasim Kadic and me on the 16th of October, 1991, which is one day after the meeting. Instead of me reading the document, I kindly ask you to read it to yourself. And once you've finished reading the first page, please tell us.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've finished reading.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the next page. Perhaps you would refer me to read it to you. Just look briefly at it. I'm not going to read everything. Basically it says here that a crisis erupted in yesterday's session and he says here that he needed to talk to me, that we had to meet at the political party level. I said that it was possible for us to agree, although I said that we were going to take numerous -- actually, put numerous actions on ice, pending the clarification of the situation. And then he said: I didn't take part in the voting nor do I wish. I asked: No, you didn't? He says: No, of course, you can read today's paper. And I would like us in the authority to reach an agreement. I thought you were all right with that. And then I have a rather lengthy statement here. Now, can we look at the next page in Serbian, where he says that their position was that opened up a space for unconstitutional conduct. Was Mr. Rasim Kadic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, look what he says here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please indicate the paragraph that he's reading. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where are you reading from? And please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we need the next page in English as well. The previous one, please. The previous one in English, the bottom of the page. And I'm reading paragraph 5 from top. [In English] In English, it is where we should see about these possible -- at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And it says that whatever comes out of that is completely legitimate. Some solutions must be sought. And I say: We have solutions for all the situations. And so on and so forth. And then I go on to say, and that's this lengthy statement, and it starts: [As read] "We also counted on the Assembly meeting in secret, but we, we secretly wanted that, to tell you the truth. I personally didn't. But my men who are clever and have less heart than I do, less soul than I do, and in politics one should neither have a heart nor a soul, they wished for it to happen."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go on, please. Next page, where he says that he was fully aware that this was opening space for unconstitutional conduct. We have to find this. Oh, here it is, number four from the top, it says --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies from the interpreters. We cannot follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
