utterances.text: Do you see that he says that this opens up space for unconstitutional conduct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Make sure the passage is in front of us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The page in the Serbian is correct. And it's his fourth statement addressed to me. Fourth from the top. I can't see it in English though. We have to look for it. In English it's towards the bottom of the page. It says: [As read] "All right. We have -- I have a statement yesterday that -- that it's an introduction into the non-institutional solution of this crisis which, in a certain way, indirectly practically this ..." and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true, Mr. Witness, that the proclamation of the autonomous region of Krajina was not the event that precipitated the crisis but the things that happened on the 15th of October?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that the certain problems arose in Kljuc due to the proclamation of the Krajina, and I think that that was the underlying reason for the worsening of relationships.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this intercept admitted into evidence under the conditions that we defined earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1747, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll have a break for half an hour. We'll resume at 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you talked about mobilisation summons, and you said that young Muslims refused to respond to the mobilisation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct. However, not young Muslims, but, rather, those who were members of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm reading this from -- [In English] "Young Muslims refused to go to wage a war in Croatia." [Interpretation] I'm not referring to the organisation of young Muslims. I was referring to young men.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, how you put it, it sounded as if there was an organisation of young Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's how you put it.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, as it's been translated now, it should read --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please wait for the interpretation to be finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we say that this mobilisation process was initiated in early 1991?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that the war in Croatia started in the summer and was in progress long before the proclamation of the Krajina and Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the transcript reflect all of what you said. When you switch to English, please put a pause before you starting reading in English. Take a look at line 22 on the previous page and check if something is missing there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes, Excellency. Excuse me. I said: And I am reading the answer of Mr. Egrlic in Krajisnik case. There were mobilisation calls, however young Muslims refused to go to a war in Croatia. Not younger. Young.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you refused -- or, rather, Muslim conscripts refused to respond to the call-up long before the proclamation of the ARK and the Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. And that was due to their being sent to the front in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but Bosnia was still in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was part of the Rump Yugoslavia, whereas Croatia had already seceded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was proclaimed but it wasn't recognised yet in 1991; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. All I know is that it was declared independent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Then you and the MBO addressed the Muslims of your municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at this document, please. It's 65 ter 21004. 21004.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this your proclamation, dated the 21st of September addressed to the Muslims of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why didn't you address all the residents of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Because the Serbs responded to mobilisation and agreed to go to fight in Croatia, and the mobilisation was for the most part organised for recruiting people to be sent to Croatia fronts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And by this announcement you put a distance between young Muslims and the JNA.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, it wasn't us who did this. It was done by those who were sending people to the front lines in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Egrlic, don't you think that defence policy of a country should be defined at a different level, not at the municipal level?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It could be regulated at the municipal level as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the event of the municipality being defended. But when you have a country at war, it is decided elsewhere.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Bosnia-Herzegovina was not at war at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could Bosnia-Herzegovina have been at war, nevertheless, because it was part of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, because Yugoslavia had already broken apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You go on to say that the war was imposed on Croatia. What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, the facts speak for themselves, that is to say that soldiers from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Serbia were being sent to Croatia where they were fighting to capture territories in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also say that in spite of that the Muslims agreed to join the Territorial Defence and the police force; is that right? The municipal army is not questionable, but Yugoslavia army is questionable?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Troops were set up at the level of municipality and were being sent to Croatia. Initially, people responded, as was customary, because we had joint Territorial Defence organisations -- organisation until they started dispatching people to Croatia and the Territorial Defence to wage war there with the aim of capturing certain areas. Then the president of the Presidency, I'm talking about Mr. Izetbegovic's address to the public, and said that the Bosniaks should not go to Croatia, and that was what prompted us to react in the same way and to draft this announcement calling upon people not to respond to the mobilisation and not to go over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So it was not you in Kljuc who did this, but it was Mr. Izetbegovic, actually, who made a distinction with regard to the JNA by saying that the Muslims shouldn't go?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. But he was speaking specifically about Croatia and he said that they should go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But in the second paragraph it says here that at the time we are -- call up all conscripts within the reserve police and Territorial Defence to respond to mobilisation --

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, interpreters couldn't hear your answer. Could you repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning this paragraph which speaks about the Bosniaks who should respond at the level of municipality. This is what this paragraph is talking about. In other words, that means that they should become members of the reserve police force and Territorial Defence. Before that, in the first paragraph, they were called not to respond, the reason being the sending of Bosniaks to Croatia, which was something that we didn't support.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask an additional question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's ascertain the situation. The Serbs respond to the calls and Mr. Izetbegovic never even invited them not to respond. They are responding, for example, in the Kljuc municipality, and so they leave to the front in Kljuc municipality. And the Muslims respond to the mobilisation calls from the Kljuc Territorial Defence and police and remain in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, from September on, any sort of response was absent. They did not respond to such calls in Kljuc or anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the able-bodied Serbs would leave Kljuc whether the Muslims ones remained in Kljuc; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. They stayed there because they did not respond and they were not engaged in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's an exhibit, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It's Exhibit P3576, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 4641, beginning in line 15, you talk about the reasons why the army became Serbian; correct? You say, and I shall read in English: [In English] [As read] "Even that the Muslims failed to respond to the call-up, the composition of the JNA became -- the JNA became composed of just one ethnic group because the Serbs would respond to the call-up so that the JNA, on the whole, became a Serbian army." [Interpretation] And then on page 4646 you say the following, beginning in line 6, response: [In English] [As read] "We were against gain such mobilisation because it wasn't in accordance with the law and the constitution of Bosnia and Herzegovina because a ministry at the level of the state had been bypassed, and mobilisation was being conducted by the local authorities in the municipality of Kljuc." [Interpretation] So you distinguish between the levels now. We have a level that you do not mention, that's the federal state; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was not operational. The Presidency which was the commander of the former JNA had stopped functioning, so that the chain of command was non-existent in practice. It had not been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Egrlic, the government was operating, the federal ministry, the General Staff as well, and isn't it the responsibility of the federal state to conduct mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: In this case, it wasn't. These were the local authorities that conducted the mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, the local authorities implemented it. Isn't it correct that mobilisation of army in case of war or an imminent threat of war is something that the federal country is responsible for?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, under normal circumstances. But we had the break-up of Yugoslavia here, and the Presidency didn't have that role anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who concluded that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, the facts speak for themselves. Slovenia was out, so was Croatia. So the former Yugoslavia had ceased to exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. In your opinion, is failing to respond to mobilisation a crime that was -- for which somebody would be punished by the laws that were then in force?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Not in this case, because in my view not even Serbs ought to have responded to these calls because they had no reason to go to the territory of another country.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But, Mr. Egrlic, you are now discussing constitutional issues, and you said you were not an expert for the constitution. The federal country still existed and so did it's army. It was legitimate. But now you declare that you know that this was not constitutional; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I suppose I have that much knowledge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, this is not a place for a constitutional or historical debate. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Not to mention the fact that Mr. Karadzic asked the witness a question, and the witness answered and then he was criticised for providing the answer as going outside his expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When the war spilled over into Bosnia, did you also refuse to receive mobilisation call-ups? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It is correct. From September onwards there was no mobilisation as far as Kljuc is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that you said that the work of the Municipal Assembly was blocked because the SDA deputies refused to participate?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please let us have a look at 22082. That's the statement, 65 ter, from 1996. Please let's have a look. I'll tell you where this is. Can we please see page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a record of your statement from 1996; correct? The last paragraph and the last sentence: "The work of the Municipal Assembly was blocked because the deputies for the SDA refused to participate," and that's followed by your signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. This is not how I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this is your statement and your signature; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It is my signature. But obviously there was some sort of error made or a mistake when this was recorded. Maybe I didn't read it when I signed it. I probably believed that what I had stated was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But is it correct that the SDA deputies had walked out of the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, when there was voting about Kljuc belonging to the Autonomous Region of Krajina. They did not want to vote on that issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the previous page in English so that we can see that particular sentence. [In English] Then it must be in the previous page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you perhaps have in mind the fact that they walked out of the Assembly when you said this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In English we need page 3, paragraph 4, so this is another page back. Paragraph 4. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: MR. KARADZIC: [Interpretation] [In English] "The work of the SO was blocked because of the refusal of the SDA deputies to participate in it." You did say that in this fashion, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I said what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that the SDA had its branches in Croatia, Slovenia, and Serbia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It had them throughout the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And as for the proclamation to sabotage the JNA, was it also sent to these organisations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you said that the war in Croatia was a war that wasn't yours and that you did not care about; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did not talk about that, whose war it is. The war didn't bring any good to anyone. It wasn't mine or yours or -- and it shouldn't have been theirs either. We only acted in the way we did. And I think there is nothing to be added or subtracted from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But during the conflicts in Croatia, you did travel to Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, not during the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During the war in Croatia, you did not travel there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And before the outbreak of the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina did you have any contacts with Croatia regarding the supply of arms and weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know that Muslim Territorial Defence was established in Kljuc, and were you involved in its establishment?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Such Territorial Defence was not established in Kljuc. What was established was the Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh. The Territorial Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina for the Kljuc municipality. And it comprised -- who was the commander, who was the chief of this Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was the late Omer Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was the Muslim's Territorial Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is not written anywhere that that was the Muslim's Territorial Defence, nor did I state anything like that anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But it was set up later, after the Serbian municipality of Kljuc was proclaimed. And after the AR of Krajina was set up, then you set up a separate Territorial Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. You were the ones who seceded by a part of the territory and formed Serbian Territorial Defence, and this Territorial Defence actually was something that followed from the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina. We were loyal to that state, and we were the continuation of that segment of state organisation in the territory of the Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that would be as if we proclaimed that we were loyal to Yugoslavia and refused to acknowledge independent Bosnia; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, it's not like that. The Serbs in Kljuc offered loyalty to the Bosniaks, and the Bosniaks refused that, as you are well aware, because they believed that loyalty not to be necessary. We had remained loyal to the state of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we were requested to sign that we were loyal to Republika Srpska and the organs which were nonexistent in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the sense in which the country had been organised before the -- all the problems that arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you know that according to the Lisbon Agreement Kljuc was to belong to Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. But that doesn't mean anything, what belonged to whom, because the agreement was not adopted and it was not in force.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you want to say that the agreement had not been reached?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, the Dayton Agreement is in force now. There were many agreements, as far as I know, but none of them were adopted, and eventually it was just the Dayton Agreement that was adopted and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Egrlic, were you parallelly organised as Muslims; you had your Crisis Staff, your units, and your institutions?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We were expelled from the municipal structures on the 7th of May so that, as I said earlier, we did not sign the declaration of loyalty, and there was no place for us anymore in the municipal organs. We then had to organise ourselves in such a manner that we could possibly give some answers, because the citizens were in great fear. The municipality was occupied, taken over. There were roadblocks and barricades at all important places. The members of the 6th Krajina Brigade from Sanski Most had done that. And this was an attempt from our part to organise ourselves in such a way so that we could communicate with the population. We opened an office in Pudin Han so that we could have such contacts, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was that an office for?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was an office of the local commune which we used to remain in touch with the population on all these various issues which were normally to be addressed by municipal bodies. Therefore, it was an attempt at overcoming the difficulties we had by installing an office where citizens could get answers to their questions and have their problems resolved.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it wasn't a local commune as such, it was, rather, their offices that you used to be in touch with the population?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was short-lived. It operated for a couple of days only. We were unsuccessful. Unfortunately, there ensued certain incidents which disrupted the affairs at the level of the Kljuc municipality. And then beyond the 27th of May, there was no possibility for anything to operate any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And when was it that you installed this office?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Around the 10th of May. Definitely after the 7th of May when the occupation took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So nobody touched you for 17 days, until the 27th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, should anyone have touched us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, no. And nobody did, in fact. There were no clashes before the 27th of May; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, there were shooting incidents. There was gun-fire, but no clashes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After the 27th of May, did you keep your Crisis Staff in June?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There was nothing in place beyond the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up, briefly, D1350. Thank you. Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the entry for the 10th of June which says that the Crisis Staff existed? Muhamed Filipovic, Omer Filipovic, and the person in charge of political affairs, Asim Egrlic. And you did confirm that you were in charge of political affairs.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I was in, but within the Territorial Defence staff there was Crisis Staff as such, because there was no opportunity to set it up. On the 27th of May, a state of war emerged for all intents and purposes. Harassment, arrests, people taken to camps. So how could you possibly under those circumstances do anything of that sort? I was, myself, detained on the 28th. Evidently whoever wrote this believed things to be that way, but that was not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at item 2, the Territorial Defence staff. And the date is the 10th of June. Can you tell us who appointed Omer Filipovic as the Territorial Defence commander?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was the commander of the Territorial Defence for Bosnia-Herzegovina, Hasan Efendic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And under 4 we can see you, Asim Egrlic, as a member of the TO staff, political affairs; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Which weapons did you have within the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. We never got the chance to organise mobilisation in order to see what sort of weapons were held by people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But tell us, some sort of weapons did reach the Muslims in Kljuc, did they not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, people procured weapons for themselves independently when the security situation became impaired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at 65 ter 17842.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 21st of June, Esad Bender produced a statement where, as you can see, he makes reference to you, right beyond Omer Filipovic, paragraph 2. Filipovic, Omer; Asim Egrlic; Ibrahim Egrlic - that's your brother, is it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was killed somewhere. Haven't found his body yet. It would be a good thing if anyone told us where both him and my other brother Mumin can be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry to here that, and it would be humane if those who know and hear you should do that. And then further down it says that as for the arming, according to what Muhamed told him, Asim together with some others, and he believed it was former police officer, went to Zagreb and brought 11- to 14.000 francs used to buy 11 submachine-guns, et cetera. Is that how it was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was a question put to you in the Brdjanin case as well, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This person Bender was killed in the meantime. If he were alive, he would be able to tell us what the circumstances were when he gave this statement. He was at Manjaca when he was killed, together with Omer Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D4440, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As I'm putting these issues to you, Witness, I'm not accusing you of anything or trying to establish what the responsibility was. I merely want to shed light on the circumstances surrounding your arrest, why was it that you were detained. Here we can see a statement where it is said specifically about the procurement of weapons, where Asim Egrlic and his brother Ibrahim, and so on and so forth, took part in that. And further down it says that they were in Switzerland and that it is believed that Alija Bilic accompanied them on this trip and on this occasion they brought over 18.000 Swiss francs that they used so buy 9 or 10 pieces of weapons, and the rest they shared between themselves. So what do you have to say to this individual placing you in the context of the procurement of weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This has nothing to do with the truth. I've never had any such dealings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D4439.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And can the speakers please pause.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 14439.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have a look. The 2nd Krajina Corps, the 11th of July, reports on the arrest in the village of Vracic, Said Halilovic, Fadil Halilovic, Rezak Halilovic, Ifet Bukvic, et cetera. In paragraph 2, it reads: "In the village of Gornji Vojici, Kljuc municipality, the Muslims procured weapons in various ways. Those who procured most weapons for the village were Arif Hukanovic and his brother Ifet Hukanovic." Further down, it goes on to say: "Furthermore, Nedzad [phoen] Djeric from Bosanski Petrovac, a haulier, also brought weapons to the village to sell it there. He brought the weapons over in a black or yellow Mercedes, and he sold the weapons at the price of 1.000 to 2.000 German marks a piece. In early 1992, there began efforts to organise themselves militarily. Organisers behind this activity were Omer Filipovic and Asim Egrlic." What do you say to this statement placing you as one of those involved in the process of military organisation?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I was a member of the BH TO staff for Kljuc municipality. I can tell you that I'm not familiar with any of the statements you've just read out about people brings in weapons, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph, it says that fundraising campaign for the procurement of weapons was launched by Ceman Fahrudin and, among others, there is also mention of Ibrahim Egrlic, your brother, are you -- from the village of Egrlic. Do you also hail from there?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it is possible that people, when they were detained at Manjaca, gave these statements under duress. Probably they were presented with template statements with the aim of indicating that there existed a very strong Territorial Defence force, which wasn't true at all. The truth is that in the municipality, a Serb TO was organised which got hold of the weapons and transported the weapons to the local commune of Ribnik, where there is 100 per cent Serb population. From that location, they distributed weapons among the Serbs and got armed. The BH TO was set up in such a way that a commander was appointed and there was a staff in place, but it did not set up any units of its own. What existed at the time were village guards, but these were volunteers standing guard to make sure that nobody slipped into their villages unnoticed, because at the time there were instances of robberies and gun-fire, et cetera. But there was no sort of organisation that would make it a military unit. It cannot possibly be stated in those terms because it's not true. I don't know of a single army in the world that could be set up on the basis of a TO commander being appointed in April and putting together an army by -- two months later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Here you have a list of names of individuals who were part of the company in his village of Hasici. It says that there were 78 armed men.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that there's 68 people here, most of them armed, some had received explosive devices, et cetera. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, you can have this on this paper whatever you want, but I will not confirm it. It was decided already before this date that certain people should be arrested and shot. In addition to these, able-bodied men, women, and children and elderly were shot as well. That is the real truth. As for these organising efforts, well, there may have been some, I wouldn't deny them, had there been time enough to do that, had -- but I can tell you that in fact there was not time enough to do that and the intelligence service was very busy at the time. There were potentials for organisation. There were able-bodied men who could have and should have responded to a call-up had one been organised, but it had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you do not deny that these Halilovics, Said, Fadil, Rezak, and others were in fact arrested; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I the only thing I know is that Halilovic and Delic, the individuals mentioned here, were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I saw that they were in Babina Dolina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You saw them being exhumed. Did you see them get killed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure they didn't kill themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that an ambush was organised on a military column in Pudin Han and Velagici at the end of May?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you that this is your viewpoint. But this ambush or attack, as you call it, was nothing of the thing. As I said, Velagici and Pudin Han were Muslims'. I said that there were village guards in place. And as the security situation deteriorated, they started standing guard in day-time as well. I heard - I wasn't eye-witness of it - as the military column passed that they opened fire on the houses nearby and on the mosque in Pudin Han, whereupon they returned fire and then things happened as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that there were people killed in the convoy, some were killed in automobiles, others in buses?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I did hear something about it, but I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So let's see what these individuals who were captured had to say about the incident. And I will read this out for the sake of everyone: "The platoon from Gornji Vojici had been engaged to stand guard before the conflict took place above the village of Vojici and Hasici. The attack on the military column in Pudin Han and Velagici had been organised by Omer Filipovic, Asim Egrlic, Cemal Velagic," and so on and so forth. Further down, the second sentence reads: "A group of some dozen individuals who were members of the company had been engaged in the transportation of explosive and laying them along the road between Laniste and Kljuc. The whole exercise didn't succeed because there wasn't enough explosives." Did you hear of this?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you see that the military organs were able to receive quite a few information about your involvement in the armed rebellion and attack on the Serbian columns. I'm not saying that the information was correct, but do you not see that these were the grounds based on which you were accused or charged, on the basis of the statements given by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I told you what the circumstances were. These Muslims were arrested, some of whom unfortunately were killed, and these statements were taken at Manjaca camp where they were held.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, they could have fabricated any other story, why this one?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, the easiest thing was to make reference to me because I was on the staff. It was only natural that they wouldn't go inventing names. It would be natural for those who were on the staff to have taken some action.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, this Official Note, which is actually not a statement given by anyone but an Official Note compiled by the army, can this be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any basis, Mr. Karadzic. You will have another opportunity to tender this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I think this is a good example of something that should be admitted even when the witness denies the allegations because it's -- it's something that's directly related to him, his name is mentioned. And its an inconsistency. We can't only admit things that the witnesses confirm, when he would be -- he's confronted with a document that directly deals with his own conduct. I think this has come up before and we've agreed that there are instances in which documents that the witness can't confirm but so closely relate to his conduct can be admitted, and I think that this is one of those.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The crux of the content were put to the witness and we have his answer in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, that's true of many, many exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And you will have another opportunity to admit this. Then --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: How would that be? That would recall us -- that would require us to call witnesses in our Defence case. I don't think that we would have to have that burden to do that if a document is otherwise admissible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Now Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think the issue here is not the one that Mr. Robinson is trying to focus on at the moment. Let me mention at the outset I'm a bit handicapped because this wasn't translated. But although the document is headed as a document of the 2nd Krajina Corps, it seems to turn out to be the case that it is a compilation of statements taken by people. So it seems that what Mr. Robinson is ignoring is this appears to fall within the ambit of the Court's previous guide-lines on statements taken. I would also indicate that I think those guide-lines have greater force when they are statements taken under conditions that not only suggest duress but where there is direct evidence of that provided by the witness. Having said all that, I don't believe that this -- under these circumstances, this document would be accorded great weight by the Court if it was admitted because of the circumstances that have been clearly outlined. But I think it was fair to note that these are the factors that bear on the consideration and assessment of admissibility in this case, not simply the one that Mr. Robinson outlined. We do agree with the general proposition that the dispositive factor may not be whether a witness agrees or disagrees with the document, depending on the nature of the document, but this document seems to involve a different issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you do not agree with the admission of this document? You object to the admission of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I believe that based on -- and I'm trying to be -- to adhere to the Court's guide-lines so we have a relatively consistent practice that the parties can count on in assessing admissibility. This one appears to me to fall under the ambit that the Court identified earlier regarding the admission of statements. This seems to be -- this seems to be a compilation of statements taken and then a different header put on them. But maybe -- as I say, I haven't got a translation, so I'm dependent upon what was read out and described and discussed during the course of the question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, very briefly. This, I think, is -- these are contemporaneous statements made during these events that I think differ -- make a differ from other third party statements that we've objected to and that you've excluded. So these are the kind of third party statements I believe that have been admitted by the Chamber when they're contemporaneous. Secondly, it's true that the circumstances under which these statements are made call into question the veracity of them, but that's strictly a matter for weight and wouldn't affect the admissibility. And I just, speaking of third party statements, recall the admission of the video of Mr. Stanic when he was being interviewed after the events, and you admitted it on the basis that the witness confirmed it, or confirmed the statements. So that was a statement of a third party made even after the events, and then you decided it should be admitted because of the issue of confirmation, which, I would submit, confirmation and contradiction is basically the same thing. So I think you've crossed the line where you've been admitting third party statements that are relevant and especially when they are contemporaneous, and I would ask you to apply that here and admit this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Sorry, but I -- and I know the Court neither wants to defer the ruling and move on or make a ruling and move on, but I just cannot let pass the suggestion that the statements extracted from people in custody, especially in the circumstances that the evidence has established in ample detail existed at the time, can be compared to comments made by SDS officials to SDS organs or to independent bodies about the objectives, about their on-going efforts, in an effort to reach and exhort their people into further activity and obedience to the on-going process. These are quite different circumstances. I'm not going to get into the full details of that. But the attempt to conflate the two and suggest that a ruling should be identical, I think, overlooks very, very significant distinctions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: On just practical questions, Mr. Robinson, you stated that Defence has no burden to introduce -- to call a witness to give some context to this document. How can I assess this document at all? You are tendering this document not for the purpose of it, not for the truth of the document, but just only to rebut the witness's evidence. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. But I think as the evidence will stand now, without any further evidence, there had been allegations made that this witness was involved in activity. You know the circumstances under which these allegations are made. The witness denies it. And that's the state of the evidence that would be -- you would have were this document to be admitted. No more than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, if the allegation is that these statements were made under duress, would that then be a question of weight alone?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: I think so, unless there was a greater showing of -- this -- that would -- that would actually implicate Rule 95, which would be a basis for excluding statements that are so unreliable that they shouldn't even be admitted at all, and I think that that's a process that requires much more evidence before a statement should be excluded on that basis. Sometimes even a hearing or at least a showing that it's come so far that it shouldn't even be considered at all. So we think in these circumstances, absent that kind of showing, that it does go to weight. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think it's a proper time to take a break now, we'll break for half an hour and resume at 1.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, excuse me. Dr. Karadzic asked me just to bring to your attention, in connection with the discussion we had about the previous document, that the information was probative not only of what conduct the witness had engaged in, if any, but what reason the authorities had for arresting him, whether it was simply because he was a Muslim or whether because they had information, reliable or otherwise, that he had engaged in some combat related activities. So he wanted me to bring that to your attention before you issue a ruling. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll defer the determination. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course that would suggest that the statements were taken before the witness's arrest, and I don't -- that doesn't seem to be the case on the basis of the dates I see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. In any event, as I already said, we'll defer the decision in order to make a more informed ruling. And in the meantime, not only because it was untranslated but also -- but also because we -- while we are considering the matter, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1748, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, you mentioned two brothers, Ibrahim and Mumin. Do you know where your brother Mumin was taken prisoner, and when?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The information I have was that he was taken prisoner in Kljuc and was transported to the Kamenica camp near Drvar. And after that nothing is known about him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was he taken prisoner in the territory of the municipality of Kljuc or in the town of Kljuc itself?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't have this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D737.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When were you released from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was transported from Manjaca to another camp, Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And from Batkovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: From Batkovic, I was exchanged, I think, on the 29th of January, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1D737 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: D1737.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D1737. It's already admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document. You went from Batkovic to Karlovac; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: To Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To Zagreb, all right. So you can see here - I can even read to you: Your brother, together with 14 other soldiers, was taken prisoner in the Galaja forest on the 6th of February, 1993. And these are very well known names, such as Ferid Hukanovic, Elvedin Keranovic, Ibrahim Keranovic, Sakib Keranovic, Hajrudin Jelecevic, and Rasim Jelecevic. They are all well-known fighters from the Kljuc and Sana Brigade.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well known for what? I haven't heard you. What are they known for?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, are these names mentioned in the previous documents as the persons who were supplying the weapons?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know why they would be well known. And where are they now?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll see what it says further on. This is the national security sector from Kljuc. The last paragraph says: What is especially interesting for the RO Kljuc is Mumin Egrlic, who is the brother of Asim Egrlic, who was the SDA president in Kljuc and the chairman of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly Executive Committee. After the war broke out --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please see the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When the war broke out, he was a member of the Bosanski Kljuc Territorial Defence Staff. He participated in an armed attack against the JNA. He was wounded, captured, and released from the Manjaca prisoners of war camp. His last known place of residence was Karlovac. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's not correct. I was in Zagreb because that's where my family was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: And as for the others, several issues are included herein.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you know where this Galaja forest is, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is the Galaja forest a place that served as a military base for the Muslim forces in the territory of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Can you please see the frame which says: In the same territory, five days ago, our PP, which means our friendly and acquaintance connection, found two tents of potato storage, potato and apple storage, [indiscernible] and fresh traces of a fairly large number of people. So you can see that he was arrested on 6th of February, 1993, after you had left for Croatia, and he was arrested as a member of a group of 15 people; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Are there any traces about where he went later on? What happened to him?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This document does not deal with that. I just want to say that the document dates from the 16th of February and that it talks about the incident in which they were taken prisoners in the Galaja forest. So you know where Galaja is, but you do not know that was a base?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It's in the direction of Sanski Most, this forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Amir Avdic is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What did he do during the war?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He left with a group of people for Bihac, and he was in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct that he left for Bihac after he had fought against Serbs in Kljuc and Sanski Most, was surrounded but he took several Serbian soldiers prisoner, and then requested, in exchange for releasing them, to be allowed free passage to the Serbian territory so he could reach Bihac?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's what I heard as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know how many fighters he had with him?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know for how many days he fought?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that either, because at the time I was already in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And was he a member of your TO staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have a look at 1D04438. We already know which minute it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just before we play that, this is a celebration in Galaja after the war. A commemoration was held of some anniversary. And is this Amir Avdic in the checkered shirt, the one who is preparing to give a speech?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The image is quite vague, but it resembles him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now play this one minute, please, so that we can hear it. The interpreters have the translation of this segment.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] "In 1992 here in this area when the Chetniks already roamed freely in Sanski Most and Kljuc, they moved against this unit and we formed it on the 30th of May, 1992, which is the day when the combatants of Kljuc and Sanski Most joined together. It is the day when we brothers in religious and neighbours found ourselves here to organise our Kljuc Sanski Most unit. "I'm happy the great number of those combatants are here among us, combatants that at the time organised themselves in a composition of Kljuc Sanski Most unit here in order to continue the tradition of the Kljuc Sanski Most unit. We fought here on the 31st and on the 1st and on 2nd so that on the 3rd of June the enemy came here with their 6th Sanski Most and 7th Kljuc light units as well as the police. They came here to these forests of Galaja to surround their unit. At the moment, we were around 2 00."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This gentleman, Amir Avdic, was he a member of this Kljuc and Sanski Most unit?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this video-clip please be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You recognise his voice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1749, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now please have a look at 1D04437.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While this is coming up, Mr. Egrlic, you were arrested on the basis of a number of indicia. Let us now go into that now because this is important for this Defence, whether that was correct or not. But there was numerous circumstantial evidence that you had committed some acts, some of which you believed probably to have been justified, and that that was the basis for your arrest; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I came to the check-point myself. No one specially arrested me. I came to the check-point and then I was taken in by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you injure, that is to say, wound yourself before that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you admitted to the Kljuc hospital?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did your colleagues from the municipality, Serbs, such as Banjac, and others, visit you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Banjac did not. But Veljko Kondic and Tihomir Dakic came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, now you see later on you were exchanged late in the year, or, rather, in early 1993, and you left for Croatia. However, in 1995 a criminal report was filed by the Kljuc Public Security Station. That means that if you were released, the proceedings had not been terminated; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you ever receive this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please have a look at this. Omer Filipovic is under number 1, and Asim Egrlic under number 2. Under number 4 we see Ibrahim Egrlic. And can we then move on, glance at other pages, so that we can see that the total number is 239.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So can we please show the last person on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 239 persons were indicted of everyone else who was arrested. So we can move on to page number 14. Yes, there it is. The last one on the list is Elkaz Bosnic. Did you know all these people?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Specifically not this last man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The transcript, at a minimum, will be confusing. But as I understood this exchange, the witness was given a brief opportunity to look at a few names, there was an emphasis on the number of people listed, and then the witness was asked if he knew all these people, which either meant the people whose names he had an opportunity to see or, more likely, the entire list. If that's the case, he needs to have an opportunity to look at the list.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you mean to ask whether witness knows 239 people? These persons, all of them?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. I meant to ask him whether he knew some of them. But I can read the names from the first page, did he know the men who are listed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Omer Filipovic, you knew him, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Iksan Zukanovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I won't ask you about your brother. Emir Kapetanovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Emir Avdic -- Amir Avdic? This is the person who we just heard speaking. Amir Avdic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He is under number 6. How about Nevzad Djeric?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Muhamed Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And so on up until number 239. Probably you didn't know some of them; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see page 16.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you meet your friends from Sanski Most in April, such as Mirzet Karabeg and others?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Which year?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In 1992. March, April, and May 1992. Did you meet them to discuss defence issues?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's possible I did, but I don't know whether these were the issues we discussed. I had nothing to do with them. They were from Sanski Most, and we were from the Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Please have a look at the second paragraph here. During April and May 1992, the representatives of the TO staff, Bosanski Kljuc, and religious officials attended a number of meetings in Sanski Most, Prijedor, and Kozarac at which a decision was made to begin an armed rebellion by which they would achieve their goals to topple the legally elected government organs, to undermine the combat power of the Serbian Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and eventually subjugate and destroy the people in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This is incorrect. This is just a number of falsifications. I don't know who wrote that, but it's obvious that it's very tendentiously written. And in a sense this does not stand.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that the relay facility near Kljuc at Kamici -- or, rather, Ramicki Kamen - that's where the relay near Kljuc was - was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph it says that the staff of your Territorial Defence issued an order that in the village of Ramici -- I'm sorry, Ramicki Kamen that a relay facility be destroyed and that this was done on the 15th of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not right at all. It's absurd. What sort of staff?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. But we see further down that on the 27th of May the staff issued an order that in the morning, at a stretch of the regional road between Kljuc and Sanski Most near Busije, and then in Ramici and Krasulje, road blocks should be set up in order to prevent any passage of police and army along that road.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which isn't true, that the order -- that the staff ordered this or that the roadblocks were erected?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was impossible for the staff to meet under those circumstances at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But is it the case that on the 27th of May incidents occurred on these locations?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Dusan Stojkovic, a police officer, assistant commander of the police stationed in Kljuc, get killed in his car in Krasulje -- or, rather, on the road between Ramici and Krasulje?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did hear of his death close to Ramici, and this was how it happened: Sabotage platoons set out to disarm someone, and that was how fire came to be opened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, three policemen were -- survived, Ljubisa, Zoran Vracar, and others who were just wounded; did you hear of them?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I did hear that there were 14 of them, that some were wounded, and that this individual was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 17 it goes on to say that those who participated in the ambush at Krasulje and Ramici were in fact ordered, those that were reported here under numbers 9 through 239, that they were ordered to open fire on the army and the police. Don't you see that the investigating bodies do have this information that the order had arrived from the staff and that it was complied with and implemented?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you wish to say that they -- their actions went above and beyond the staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not saying anything. But the area where this took place was a location when -- where village guards were organised, first at night, and then in day-time as well. And this was local Bosnia population. Krasulje was also 100 per cent Bosniak. There were no attacks mounted by the Bosniaks. An announcement was broadcast on Radio Kljuc to the effect that actions would be taken to disarm people, to have weapons surrendered, and that any and all measures will be employed to that effect, and that a sabotage platoon headed off for Krasulje. This is information that I learned at a later date, and I can't confirm that they're one hundred per cent true. I wasn't a participant in that event. But I heard of it, and I told you what I knew of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 27th of May, there were five or six incidents taking place during the same day in the municipality of Kljuc; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, the Serbian army did carry out raids from several directions into that area, and people were defending their homes. This wasn't the case of people going elsewhere to do anything. The incidents happened right by their homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Egrlic, does a main road, a trunk road, pass through Velagici?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was not fire opened on that road and on the military column that was passing along?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, don't you know that there were columns after columns passing along that road, firing upon the local population and the mosque, not just in Velagici, but in Velecevo and other locations along the road. This made the situation unsettling and probably that was the cause why the incident took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And people were killed on the bus; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, so I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statements, you say that on the 1st of June, so not much later, civilians, Muslims were killed in a school in Velagici; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, so I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And those documents that were admitted here, don't they refer to that very incident?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Not "documents," but "headstones."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is just for the record: 65 ter 23653, it was admitted as a P here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Don't you know, Mr. Egrlic, that Serb investigating bodies did carry out an investigation into these events?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did here of it during one of my testimonies. I also heard that they were held in a prison for 18 days and then released.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you were released as well, but you were charged, too. Release does not equal termination of proceedings.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, 130 people were killed there. Had someone's chickens been killed, that would have warranted a more serious detention, and longer than 18 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I do believe that at some point we will admit the documents underlying the investigation that I've referred to, and these people were tried, after all. It wasn't the way you put it. Do you mean to say, then, that Velagici were under attack simply because they happened to have a road passing through along which an army was going from Knin to Yugoslavia and that the fact that there's a column there, it constitutes a legitimate target?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There was provocation on a daily basis and on that day, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said a moment ago that there had not been that much organisation or weapons. Do you mean to say that the only thing you had was this staff, and that the 200 men, Abdic's men, were not combatants?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. What I can tell you is what happened up to when I was arrested. What happened then, after my arrest, how many people got organised and involved, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the Una and the Sana valleys, or, rather, in the Sana valley where Kljuc is, was there an organisation of the Patriotic League even before the war? Was it not organised under the direction and supervision of Sefer Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that they were able to go about this activity unbeknownst to you as a prominent member of the staff?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that it was a covert activity. I'd rather say that there was no such activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you regularly in touch with your head office in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Whatever necessitated contacts with the party could be addressed with them up until, let's say, September of 1991. All communication was down thereafter and we weren't able to receive TV or radio signals because the relay had been rerouted to receive news from Belgrade and Banja Luka. Therefore, we had no contacts with Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now that you've mentioned relay, I see that you mentioned the issue in other testimonies as well. Can you tell us, when was it that TV Sarajevo made it impossible for the Serbs to view TV Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It was in 1991, Mr. Egrlic. Tell us, in April of 1992, who was the person in charge of Radio Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Azemir Burzic, who was later replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Azemir Burzic or Buzanic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Burzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A Muslim, therefore. Until which day in April?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Is it your evidence, then, that Sefer Halilovic did not supervise the establishment of the Patriotic League in your region?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I told you that I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D4282.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Have a look at what Sefer Halilovic has to say. He is developing certain views here, and it was signed by Sefer Halilovic in September of 1992. In paragraph 1, he says as follows: [As read] "I have followed," he says, "the development of the BH Army in the Bihac region with full attention, and in organising its embryo of the Patriotic League I was in the region personally on six occasions; therefore, the situation in the wider region from the pre-war days till today is completely familiar to me. I was even in a position to alert the government organs in that region to the fact that armed combat was being obstructed. Since they waited for a rather long period of time while the war was ranging in all of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, they were still negotiating with the aggressor in this region." So is it not true that up until the 27th of May you did not in fact have any hostilities in your area, at a time when a war was raging elsewhere in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's Sefer's statement. I don't know what he had in mind. But the fact of the matter is that we did not have any sort of conflicts or confrontations, that we were trying to reach an agreement over everything, and to thus preserve the peace.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did not have any conflicts with the Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: With no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the next paragraph. We will come to that issue. But do you not agree with me that in the first paragraph he does object to the fact that negotiations had been going on for so long with the aggressor? So does he think that your neighbours from Kljuc were the aggressor?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: You should put that question to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In paragraph 2, he goes on to say that they relied on proven, qualified, and capable personnel, and primarily these were individuals from the Patriotic League. And he makes reference to Osmanagic, Drekovic, et cetera. So do you have any doubts about the fact that in the Sana and Una valleys Sefer Halilovic did appear on six occasions to supervise the establishment of the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: You asked me the question already. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the document admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. This is an example of wasting time. Witness already said to ask Mr. Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't think that we can secure his appearance here. He will not appear of his own accord, that's for sure. But this is -- this refutes what the witness has been saying all along, i.e., that there had been no organisation. And this is an official document. It is not a statement. It's an official act produced by the staff of the Supreme Command of the armed forces with reference to its organisation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There's no basis to admit this. We'll not admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's see if we can agree on what he says here, that at a time when a war was raging throughout the BiH, you kept on negotiating --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is again a waste of time. Witness denied he knows anything about this content. Then you -- it's time for you to move to next topic. Just put your case to the witness. And having heard his answer, you proceed to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Excellency, if you had more confidence in me, you would see that I am moving to a different topic. But the queue I wanted to give was that they had been negotiating for two months, and I wanted to address the issue of the relationship between the Muslims and the Serbs while the war was already on. That is the topic, the new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What is your question for the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. The walking out of the members of MBO and SDA of a session, was that taken as a justification for illegal construction works in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at document P3458. P3458.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You can see here in the heading that it reads "Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bosanski Kljuc Municipal Assembly," so this is the Bosnian municipality?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: What do you mean Bosniak? You are claiming something that has absolutely no connection to reality. There was one municipality of Kljuc. It was not called either Bosniak or Serb. This is the year 1992, 31st of January, there was no question of there being a Muslim municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But we have this document in front of us and it says Bosanski Kljuc municipality as opposed to the Serbian Kljuc. Now, let us see what was the reason for the deputies to walk out, and it says, in paragraph 2: "The reason for leaving the session this time was the fact that the SDS Assemblymen in the Joint Assembly rejected objections to the agenda that were based on a request to protect legality."
