And the next paragraph: "There were reasoned requests by SDA and MBO for the item of illegal construction in Kljuc municipality not to be removed from the agenda," et cetera. So you had a Joint Assembly, a Serbian Assembly, and a Bosnian Assembly, as was the case throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, that was not the case. There was only one Assembly, and eventually we had only Serbian Assembly. There was no Muslim Assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it says quite the opposite here.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here, Assemblymen of the Bosanski Kljuc Municipal Assembly. Do you recognise these signatures? One of them is Asim Egrlic. Do you see a man called Memisevic or Hrmcic? Look a little bit to the -- closer to the top. It says: "At the second session, held immediately after withdrawing from the work of the Joint Assembly, the Bosanski Kljuc examined in detail the situation that had arisen and established that the move was made -- that was made was the only possible thing to do, as the unruliness and lawlessness had to be finally pointed out, highlighting them now as the basis and the only cause for the cessation of the work of the Joint Assembly, and not political reasons which are constantly being highlighted by the SDS." So you really believe that illegal construction works was sufficient reason for you to walk out of the Assembly, of the Joint Assembly?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. It is possible that there was participation and debate about this item of the agenda, but I think that the Assembly suspended its work until April. There may have been disagreements on certain issues, but the Assembly continued to operate with regard to other issues that requested the consent of all political parties.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please ask questions one by one. Mr. Egrlic, do you recognise your signature there? It seems to be the second item on the right part. We can zoom in. Second row, on the right column.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is it your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is already in evidence as P3458. So although it says here immediately after abandoning the work in the Joint Assembly, you nevertheless continued to work occasionally in the Joint Assembly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that was the situation that prevailed until the beginning of May; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka, or the ARK, adopted conclusions to the effect that they called upon people not to move out from the Autonomous Region of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that people of all religions and ethnicities, before the war broke out, because of the tensions and the war in Croatia, were actually leaving all municipalities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, there were individual departures. However, mass departures took place as of the 1st of June, as far as Kljuc was concerned, and everybody left by September, with the exception of a couple of hundred people who remained behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that before conflicts and confrontations broke out in Kljuc, Serbs as well were moving out of Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is possible that there were individual cases. It was a process that was an on-going one from the previous war, because the living conditions were harsh. People emigrated to other countries in search for work and better living conditions. So it was only natural and normal for people to be leaving.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that Serbs didn't suffer from any sort of fear?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think they had any reason to be afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Between January and April 1992, would you say that more Serbs left during that period than before? You were the president of the municipal government; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is. And it is possible that that was the case, but we did not make a survey of the situation in order to be able to tell you exactly how many people had left.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that Republika Srpska under the Lisbon Agreement had a right to have its own police force?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: According to all plans, including the Dayton Agreement, was Republika Srpska entitled to have its independent police force and if that is still the case today?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I know that it has its own police force today, but I cannot comment on the rest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How relevant is it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellency, you really have no faith in me. I'm exactly moving to a new topic. This is the issue of insignia, and the witness pointed this out as a major stumbling block.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right, you don't know about that. But you did testify to the fact that you had been told -- but first of all, let me tell you this: Is it true that the police force was divided in late March or early April?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the last part of the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The total rifts in the police force happened after the 7th of May. After the 7th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You helped us elucidate one thing. So Banjac and you and the others went to see the chief of the Banja Luka region CSB Mr. Zupljanin. Did that take place in April, or when?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember the exact date, whether it was in April or in May. I would have thought it was May.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So war is everywhere in Bosnia, whereas you as a member of a mixed delegation are paying a visit to Mr. Zupljanin to discuss the issue of the police force; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you say that Mr. Zupljanin told you that he wasn't able to do anything about it, that that was a decision taken at a higher level; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that the decision and the agreement to divide the police was taken on or around 27th of March, and that Mr. Mandic had sent a dispatch referring to the Lisbon Agreement in order to have two police forces formed?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. You are talking about an agreement that has not been adopted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave that aside. As far as Serbs are confirmed [as interpreted], this agreement was adopted. Without it, it wouldn't have been any independent Bosnia. Now, when you said "this higher level," what did you mean by that, when you said that this decision came from a higher level?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know. Mr. Zupljanin said that. I suppose he was referring to the government or the Assembly. It is well known which bodies are -- can make such decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If Stojan Zupljanin told you that it had come from a higher level, did you try to inquire with your police commander in Kljuc to find out whether he had received this dispatch, where it came from, and what was the basis for separating the police force into two entities?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. I didn't receive that. I didn't inquire about that. I know that on the 7th of May, when the 6th Krajina Brigade entered the town, flags were hoisted, the plaque on the police building was changed, and it was now called a Serbian police. There were Serbian flags on all official buildings, et cetera. Now, the thing -- this thing with relation to our visit to Banja Luka was just a matter of formality which was arranged by Mr. Kondic and Banjac in order to persuade us that nothing could be done and that was the end of story and that the police would have to be divided and that one part of it will become the Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In one of your earlier statements, you said that some of the local Bosniaks were mobilised by force but later managed to escape and had to face consequences. Were they mobilised by a force by the JNA or by the Serbian police?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, that had to do with this part that deals with mobilisation or membership in the TO or JNA. It wasn't about the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that this decision as well, concerning the symbols and insignia just, like the previous decision concerning the integration into the Republika Srpska, was delayed by the Serbs, because, as you said, the real rift happened after the 7th of May?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They delayed it for the whole period between March and May; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, did you, the Muslim Bosniak leadership, did you ask the -- ask the Bosnians to --

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can Mr. Karadzic please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, this will be your last question. Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we can briefly look at 65 ter 22083. It's your 1997 statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear your last question, so could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question was: Did you ask the Bosniak police officers, Muslims, to take a leave of absence so that that would give you time for reaching an agreement with the SDS concerning the symbols and the insignia? This is what is says on page 4. Did you request that or not? You said you didn't.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, they had already been sent on leave, so I don't remember whether we specifically suggested this course to them, but it was already a fait accompli.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The penultimate passage says -- [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You are too fast and we didn't get translation. We'll continue tomorrow. Mr. Egrlic, we'll adjourn for today and continue tomorrow morning. In the meantime, you are required not to discuss with anybody else about your testimony. Do you understand that, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, 9.00.
